      <content name="altTitle">Leg &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;Cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;</content>
      <content name="FullSummary">What are &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;?&lt;p&gt;&lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;Muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; are sudden, involuntary contractions or spasms in one or more of your &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt;. They are very common and often occur after exercise. Some people get &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, especially leg &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, at night. They can be painful, and they may last a few seconds to several minutes.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;You can have a &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramp&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; in any &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscle&lt;/span&gt;, but they happen most often in the:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Thighs&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Feet&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Hands&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Arms&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Abdomen&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Area along your ribcage&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;What causes &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;?&lt;p&gt;Causes of &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; include:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Straining or overusing a &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscle&lt;/span&gt;. This is the most common cause.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Compression of your nerves, from problems such as a spinal cord injury or a pinched nerve in the neck or back&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Dehydration&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Low levels of electrolytes such as magnesium, potassium, or calcium&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Not enough blood getting to your &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Pregnancy&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Certain medicines&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Getting dialysis&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;Sometimes the cause of &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; is unknown.&lt;/p&gt;Who is at risk for &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;?&lt;p&gt;Anyone can get &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, but they are more common in some people:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Older adults&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;People who are overweight&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Athletes&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Pregnant women&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;People with certain medical conditions, such as thyroid and nerve disorders&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;When do I need to see a health care provider for &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;?&lt;p&gt;&lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;Muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; are usually harmless, and they go away after a few minutes. But you should contact your health care provider if the &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Are severe&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Happen frequently&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Don't get better with stretching and drinking enough fluids&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Last a long time&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Are accompanied by swelling, redness, or a feeling of warmth&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Are accompanied by &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscle&lt;/span&gt; weakness&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;What are the treatments for &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;?&lt;p&gt;You usually don't need treatment for &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;. You may be able to find some relief from &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; by:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Stretching or gently massaging the &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscle&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Applying heat when the &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscle&lt;/span&gt; is tight and ice when the &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscle&lt;/span&gt; is sore&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Getting more fluids if you are dehydrated&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;If another medical problem is causing the &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, treating that problem will likely &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;help&lt;/span&gt;. There are medicines that providers sometimes prescribe to prevent &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, but they are not always effective and may cause side effects. Talk to your provider about the risks and benefits of medicines.&lt;/p&gt;Can &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; be prevented?&lt;p&gt;To prevent &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, you can:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Stretch your &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt;, especially before exercising. If you often get leg &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; at night, stretch your leg &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt; before bed.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Drink plenty of liquids. If you do intense exercise or exercise in the heat, sports drinks can &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;help&lt;/span&gt; you replace electrolytes.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;</content>

    <document rank="1" url="https://medlineplus.gov/heatillness.html">
      <content name="title">Heat Illness</content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Heat Exhaustion</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Hot (Temperature)</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Sunstroke</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Heat stroke</content>
      <content name="FullSummary">&lt;p&gt;Your body normally cools itself by sweating.  During hot weather, especially when it is very humid, sweating just isn't enough to cool you off. Your body temperature can rise to dangerous levels and you can develop a heat illness.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Most heat illnesses happen when you stay out in the heat too long. Exercising and working outside in high heat can also lead to heat illness. Older adults, young children, and those who are sick or overweight are most at risk. Taking certain medicines or drinking alcohol can also raise your risk.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Heat-related illnesses include:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Heat stroke - a life-threatening illness in which body temperature may rise above 106 °F (41 °C) in minutes. Symptoms include dry skin, a rapid, strong pulse, dizziness, nausea, and confusion. If you see any of these signs, get medical &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;help&lt;/span&gt; right away.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Heat exhaustion -  an illness that can happen after several days of exposure to high temperatures and not enough fluids. Symptoms include heavy sweating, rapid breathing, and a fast, weak pulse. If it is not treated, it can turn into heat stroke.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Heat &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps - muscle&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt; pains&lt;/span&gt; or spasms that happen during heavy exercise. You usually get them in your abdomen, arms, or legs.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Heat rash - skin irritation from excessive sweating. It is more common in young children.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;You can lower your risk of heat illness by drinking fluids to prevent dehydration, replacing lost salt and minerals, and limiting your time in the heat.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Centers for Disease Control and Prevention&lt;/p&gt;</content>
